attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Will eventually pop' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The normalised version keeps it exactly.

contract.note: Reading 'pop' as a broad, severe collapse in valuations and financing is the ordinary reading. Geographic scope is inferred from context, and a regional reading could change the result. Requiring an impossibility to contradict an 'eventually' claim is appropriate.

evidence.note: A two-week October selloff in AI segments, with hyperscalers down 5.9%. This is stress, not a broad collapse.
Venture funding through Q3 2026 was on pace for a record, led by AI mega-rounds. That is not a financing collapse.
Secondary report, citing Reuters, of a 40% STAR50 drop in China. This is a regional episode and does not establish the broader collapse.

reviews.rationale: This is an undated forecast. By the cutoff the evidence shows an October selloff and a Chinese regional decline, but funding remains at record levels and no broad, severe collapse is shown. Not having popped yet does not disprove 'eventually', so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Can't last' is a firm claim about the future with no horizon. The normalised version leaves out the normative 'should have said' and the separate claim about analyst upgrades, but it captures what he commits to: the neoclouds are risky and cannot last.

contract.note: Using bankruptcy, liquidation or a necessary rescue as the endpoint for 'can't last' is a fair, ordinary reading. Requiring both named companies to be addressed is fair. Under any reasonable endpoint the result is unresolved for now.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own Q2 2026 results show continued operations, a widening net loss and higher interest expense. This is a company disclosure and settles nothing.
IREN's own FY26 results say capacity is largely sold out and report a large net loss. This is a company disclosure, and neither failure nor sustainability is shown.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. By the cutoff neither CoreWeave nor IREN has failed or needed a rescue, and neither has shown a lasting end to its alleged dependence on circular financing. Continuing to operate cannot disprove an open-ended forecast, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The normalised version keeps the qualifier 'the underlying economics suggest'. That is an inference with graded confidence, not a flat assertion, and 'any kind of financial sense' has no defined measure.

contract.note: The contract scores a hedged statement as a firm observation. It also imposes a Q1 2026 period and a viability test, neither of which the speaker supplied. The plain-reading rule does not apply to hedged language.

evidence.note: Secondary report of the Midjourney CEO saying the company is profitable. This is a company self-report with no defined basis or subscription-level costs. It is a candidate counterexample, but it cannot be scored here.

reviews.rationale: 'Suggest' hedges the universal claim, and 'makes any kind of financial sense' names no measure, so under policy it is not scored. The Midjourney profitability report would be a material counterexample to a firm version of the claim, but it is an unverified company account.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He reports the Zillow figure from his own earlier reporting on an internal deck, and he endorses it.

semantics.note: Mostly faithful. It leaves out the 'millions of dollars a year' spending claim for Zillow, but the contract covers that part.

contract.note: Reading the 29,000 hours as added monthly human review time is ordinary, and so is treating 'slop' as rhetoric. The target window is inferred but reasonable.

evidence.note: Zillow's May 2026 shareholder letter claims 40% more code per engineer at the same or higher quality. This is management's own claim, and code volume is not delivered output. It does not address review hours.
Zillow's June 2026 employee accounts describe faster experimentation. They are company-sourced, dated after the target window and narrow in scope.

reviews.rationale: The 29,000-hour figure and the spending figure trace only to Zitron's own reporting. No independent records verify them or refute them. Zillow's self-reported productivity gains are company claims, not independent findings, and no comparable engineering data settle the broader claim, so it is unresolved.
